sourceCoverage.note: No company disclosure is used for either grid-policy item.
ERCOT and PJM original pages were read; both describe regulator or grid-operator actions, not individual project approval.
No earnings release or call supports the selected policy items.
The pages were read for interconnection and operating constraints. Neither grants a permit, a MW allocation, energization or commercial operation.
ERCOT identifies the Texas governor and PUCT process; PJM identifies the intended FERC filing. Their disclosed measures are RFI/proposal status, not effective new rules.
No binding final technical standard was read in this bounded review; PJM's ride-through measure remains proposed.
Neither selected item identifies a customer contract or supplier partnership as evidence.
The selected public items rely on grid-operator originals rather than media reporting.

change.description: ERCOT publicly issued a separate RFI for developers of 25MW-plus data centers pursuing system interconnection, adding state and community impact data requirements beyond the existing Batch Zero verification notice.

impact.affected: Texas data-center developers pursuing ERCOT interconnection at 25MW or above
impact.consequence: The RFI can add information and regulatory-process dependencies around water, cooling, onsite generation, public support and ownership before developers' projects are evaluated; it does not approve any project.

sources.finding: ERCOT says the RFI applies to all data-center developers at 25MW or above pursuing ERCOT interconnection; it lists submission by October 12 and an ERCOT/PUCT analysis by December 10, without projects or MW.

primaryAttempts.note: Original ERCOT legal-policy page read directly.

change.description: PJM's original post describes a new proposed reliability requirement for large computational loads to ride through normally cleared disturbances, addressing a constraint separate from prior project-specific interconnection records.

impact.affected: PJM large computational loads, including data centers, and their interconnection design and operating plans
impact.consequence: The proposal can impose reliability-design and transition requirements on large-load facilities if advanced; it does not allocate capacity, approve a project or establish a final standard.

sources.finding: PJM says it proposes ride-through requirements for large computational loads including data centers, will discuss transition planning for existing facilities and plans a November FERC filing; the source calls the measure a proposal.
